steps.what: Report the printer fault and device id
Match the peripheral to the inventory
Sign the fault codes vendors may take
Queue a fault the signed codes cover
Repair the printer under the signed fault

tasks.design: A system user reports a printer or other peripheral with a device id on the {HELPDESK}. The architect signs the fault codes a vendor may take. Those codes queue on {WORKFLOW}. Anything else is a site visit. A replacement or a connection change needs a signed decision for that device id. The vendor engineer repairs only what was signed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Faults arrived as mail and corridor requests, so a vendor visit could not tell a known jam from a device that had to be moved.
tasks.enabler_now: A device id and a short fault code can be matched to an inventory row and to a signed code list.
tasks.still_hard: A fault that is not on the list, and any change to how the device is connected, still need the architect.
tasks.human_edge: The architect signs the code list and decides replacements and connection changes on site.

ambition.what: Small sites can queue a known printer fault without waiting for a visit

tasks.altitude: Known codes stop being a trip. The architect can refuse a replacement that names no device, and still walks the faults the list does not cover.

reach.task: Repair or replace only the device and action that were signed
reach.learn: Which fault codes are in force and which device ids need a visit

evidence.claim: Printer care in a mid-size firm is a ticket plus a visit. A short list of fault codes can be queued. The rest cannot.
Digest [S1] and [S2] say a service desk can suggest a ticket category for a person to review. That sorts a printer ticket. It does not repair the device.
Digest [S15] is a vendor self-service claim of fewer tickets, and no baseline was published, so it is not a reason to drop the printer visit.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. A peripheral ticket stores device id and fault code, not what was printed.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so a fault code may queue a vendor but may not change the network connection unattended.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task is coordination of peripheral maintenance, not a redesign of the network. The vendor engineer does the repair.
Input contract: device id, site, fault code, requester. Producer is the system user. A report with no device id is returned. A code that is not on the signed list is not queued.

The meeting-heavy prior does not fit as sit-down meetings. Most of that time is a floor visit and a vendor repair, which stay in person. Use the helpdesk's own queue before custom code. Print content is not logged, so this is not staff monitoring.
unknowns: Which peripherals have no device id.
Which fault codes the vendor contract already includes.
Who may sign a replacement when the architect is away.
research_questions: What share of printer faults repeats a code already on the list?
How often does a queued fault still become a visit?

already_counted.description: Architect's time on faults the code list does not cover
Architect still checks the inventory match

incremental.description: Add a fault code when the same jam repeats and the vendor can take it
System users resubmit a report that has no device id

approvals.approved_version: fault-code rule signed for this period
site decision signed for this device id and action

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most printer faults have no signed code, so the queue rarely runs and the site visit is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The architect stops visiting every printer and keeps the decision on replacements and any change to how a device is connected.
reach: Vendor engineers receive only the fault codes signed for this period.
System users see a ticket state instead of sending a second mail.
skills_to_grow: Write a printer fault code as a rule a queue can apply.
Visit when the code is not on that rule, and sign any connection change.
role.ambitious_version: A known printer fault reaches the vendor without a visit, and every replacement names a device id.
